section_summary: This section contains U.S. Embassy Tokyo's reporting on internal and foreign affairs of Japan during the late summer of 1937, comprising the concluding lists of despatches and telegrams for July 1937, the complete monthly report for August 1937 (Report No. 131, transmitted by Despatch No. 2584), and the initial part of the monthly report for September 1937 (Report No. 132, transmitted by Despatch No. 2633). The reports focus heavily on the rapid expansion of the Sino-Japanese conflict following the Marco Polo Bridge and Shanghai outbreaks, detailing Japanese land offensives, naval blockades, and aerial bombing campaigns across China. They also document extensive diplomatic representations by the United States, Great Britain, France, and other powers concerning non-combatant safety and foreign property, alongside Japan's domestic wartime legislation, financial emergency budgets, and shifting relations with the Soviet Union, Germany, and Italy.

subfiles.about: Lists of despatches (Nos. 2489 to 2518) and telegrams (Nos. 171 to 239) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during July 1937.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains the concluding lists of official despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State by the American Embassy in Tokyo during the month of July 1937, forming the final part of the Embassy's monthly report for that month. Despatches No. 2489 through 2518 cover routine matters such as visa reports, cotton textile regulations, salmon fisheries, and the opening stages of the North China Incident. Telegrams No. 171 through 239 document fast-moving developments surrounding the Amur River border clash, the outbreak and escalation of the North China situation, narcotics control, foreign exchange restrictions, and the disappearance of Amelia Earhart.
subfiles.title: Despatches and Telegrams Sent to the Department During July, 1937 (Enclosure to Despatch No. 2524)

subfiles.about: Comprehensive monthly report on political, international, military, and economic developments in Japan during August 1937, transmitted with lists of August despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 131 detailing Japan's internal and external affairs during August 1937, dominated by the outbreak of major hostilities in Shanghai and North China. The report outlines U.S. and multi-power diplomatic representations regarding the neutralization of Shanghai, the protection of foreign embassies and non-combatant areas in Nanking, casualties aboard the USS Augusta, and Japan's coastal blockade of China. It reviews Japan's relations with Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, and Soviet Russia, noting severe friction over the machine-gunning of British Ambassador Knatchbull-Hugessen and rumors regarding the Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact. Domestic coverage highlights the Diet's 71st session passing emergency wartime economic controls, tax increases, and supplementary military budgets exceeding 400 million yen, alongside court-martial sentencing of General Mazaki and civilian ringleaders of the February 26 Incident. Appended lists index Embassy despatches Nos. 2519–2564 and telegrams Nos. 240–333 sent during August 1937.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2584: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of August, 1937 (Report No. 131)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Monthly report on political, diplomatic, and military conditions in Japan during September 1937, covering the expansion of the war in China, extensive foreign protests, and Diet proceedings.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 132 detailing Japanese internal and foreign affairs during September 1937, marked by escalating military operations across North, Central, and South China. The Embassy details vigorous American, British, and French diplomatic protests against indiscriminate Japanese aerial bombing of Nanking, Canton, and missionary hospitals, as well as debates over third-party shipping rights under Japan's coastal blockade. The report examines international developments including the League of Nations' condemnation of aerial bombardments, Japan's apology for the wounding of the British Ambassador, tensions with Soviet Russia following the Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, and anti-communist alignment with Italy. Coverage of internal political affairs records the convening of the Diet's 72nd emergency session and ministerial addresses by Foreign Minister Hirota justifying military actions before the text breaks off.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2633: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of September, 1937 (Report No. 132)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington
